To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Apache throughput is limited by the number of concurrent requests that can be handled by the server, which is in turn limited by the CPU and the disk I/O bandwidth; (2) the throughput of Apache can be improved by increasing the server's ability to handle concurrent requests, and (3) the throughput of the server can also be improved by decreasing the time spent by the server on each request
the performance of the Apache Web Server can be improved by 61% using 6 general purpose techniques that reduce the number of kernel events and improve the efficiency of the kernel event processing.

(1) the throughput of Apache is bottlenecked by the number of processes it creates to service requests and by the amount of time it spends waiting for the processes to complete, and (2) the throughput can be improved by 61% by (a) reducing the number of processes by using a single process to service all the requests, (b) eliminating the process wait time by using threads to service requests, and (c) eliminating the time to create a thread by reusing the thread

the performance bottleneck of a server is usually not in the server itself, but in the system that the server is running on.
a detailed understanding of the system behavior, especially the behavior of the operating system, is essential in order to improve performance.
